During that work the reviewer asked that *all* algorithms in the codebase be \\\"truly general\\\" — built from the smallest possible meaningful substitutions (rules) via actual reasoning, rather than memoization (fixed lookup tables / per-case keyword whitelists).\\n\\nThe #423 installation-conversion algorithm is architecturally general (single install-step IR + format-agnostic renderers, no per-repository lookup table — the 100 regression repos all flow through the same pipeline). But while implementing it, several memoization-flavored heuristics were noticed across the solver that deserve their own generalization pass. Filing here so #424 stays scoped to the README↔script conversion task.\\n\\n## What \\\"memoization vs reasoning\\\" means here\\n\\nA memoized recognizer answers by matching against a hardcoded enumeration (extend the list → support one more case). A reasoning recognizer derives the answer compositionally from structure, so unseen-but-well-formed inputs are handled without editing a table.\\n\\n## Concrete spots observed\\n\\n1. **Command recognition is a fixed prefix whitelist.** `src/solver_handlers/installation_conversion.rs::looks_like_command` accepts a line only if it starts with one of an enumerated `PREFIXES` set (`apt `, `brew `, `cargo `, `npm `, …). Any tool not in the list is silently dropped from the IR. A structural recognizer (token shape, code-span provenance in Markdown, pipe/`&&` composition) would reason about whether a line *is a command* rather than memorizing tool names.\\n2. **Step descriptions are a fixed mapping.** `describe_command` maps substrings (`git clone` → \\\"Clone the repository\\\", etc.) to prose. General intent inference from the command verb/object would scale beyond the enumerated cases.\\n3. **Intent dispatch is a fixed ordered table.** `src/solver_dispatch.rs::SPECIALIZED_HANDLERS` is a hand-ordered list of `(intent, handler)` pairs; each new task class appends one entry. This is the central place where \\\"one solution per memorized intent\\\" lives, versus synthesizing a handler from smaller reusable rule primitives (the meta-algorithm direction from #423).\\n\\n## Proposed direction\\n\\n- Replace the command whitelist with a structural command recognizer (provenance- + shape-based) and measure it against the existing #423 regression corpus (must stay green) plus adversarial prose lines.\\n- Generalize `describe_command` to derive descriptions from the parsed verb/object instead of a substring table.\\n- Audit the remaining specialized handlers for memoized keyword lists that could be expressed as composable rules, and prototype expressing one existing handler purely through the #423 meta-algorithm rule primitives as a proof of concept.\\n\\n## Acceptance criteria\\n\\n- A written audit listing each handler that relies on a fixed enumeration vs. compositional rules.\\n- At least the installation-conversion command recognizer generalized away general meta algorithm (issue #559): how our Formal AI turns any message into a solved, link-native knowledge base. Every prompt is formalized to one meaning record, expanded into an explicit problem frame that enumerates every detected need, decomposed by a recursive bounded downward pass into a work-unit tree whose atomic leaves each map to a method, accounted for in a need-satisfaction ledger so no need is dropped, resolved against a method registry derived from the live dispatch code, executed through the registry-backed method dispatcher, reasoned about in the open with white-box reasoning attached to every recursive step in both directions (the downward decomposition and the upward construction that composes children back into each answer), traced leaf by leaf so the method the single data-driven registry authority resolves for each atomic leaf is auditable, projected back into the answer from the append-only event log, and finally distilled into a proposal-only skill-accumulation ledger that turns each satisfied need into a candidate reusable skill and each blocked need into a curriculum item — with no neural inference and no skill ever auto-promoted without review. The recipe is grounded: tests/unit/specification/recursive_core_recipe.rs asserts the live source still defines every function and step named here, so this file always describes how the meta core was produced, not stale prose.\"\n./data/meta/recursive-core-recipe.lino:6:  generalization \"To extend the meta algorithm to a new class of tasks, do not add a bespoke branch: instead make the new behaviour fall out of the twelve ordered steps below. Formalize the impulse to a meaning record, let the problem frame surface its needs structurally, let the recursive downward pass decompose it until each leaf is single-method solvable, register the resolving handler as one more method in the catalogue, let the registry-backed dispatcher execute the selected method, let the ledger prove every need was addressed, let the method-selection trace record which method the sole registry authority resolves for each leaf, and let the skill-accumulation ledger turn the outcome into proposed reusable skills and a curriculum of what is still unsolved. The specific algorithm becomes data (a method record) reached by the same general loop, so the core reasons about and executes through its method set instead of growing new hardcoded intents. Recognisers ask the lexicon for a *meaning* by role\n     (`lexicon().meanings_with_role(ROLE_…)`) or load a named vocabulary\n     (e.g. `seed::terminal_command_vocabulary()`); they never hardcode\n     per-language phrase arrays or branch on literal user phrasings.\n   - **Responses / output.** Every user-facing answer string is a template in\n     `data/seed/multilingual-responses.lino` looked up by intent\n     (`seed::response_for(intent, lang)` in Rust, `answerFor(...)` in the\n     worker). Code fills placeholders like `{command}`; it does not embed the\n     surrounding prose.\n   - **Web front-end (React).** Every string the user sees in `src/web/app.js`\n     — permission-panel titles, button labels, status words, onboarding copy,\n     system messages — is a catalog entry in `src/web/i18n-catalog.lino`, looked\n     up at render time via `t(\"<key>\", params)` (the `window.FormalAiI18n`\n     engine). Never pass a prose string literal as a child of `h(...)`; route it\n     through `t(...)` so it follows the active UI language and fills placeholders\n     like `{granted}/{total}`.\n\n   The principle is **meanings ↔ naturalization**: a *meaning* (a slug grounded\n   in seed data) can be *naturalized* into a natural-language surface, and any\n   natural-language word can be *formalized* back into a meaning. Code only ever\n   moves meanings around; the words live in the seed. Add a new cue or answer by\n   editing the `.lino` file and declaring the role/intent — not by typing a\n   phrase into `src/*.rs` or `formal_ai_worker.js`.\n\n   This is enforced by CI, not just convention:\n   - **Total reference-closure gate** (`tests/unit/total_closure.rs` →\n     `scripts/audit-total-closure.py`, run by `cargo test --tests`). Every bare\n     value token in any `data/seed/*.lino` must resolve to a defined meaning, a\n     declared role, a cached dictionary lemma, or a Wikidata id. New vocabulary\n     that resolves to nothing fails the build. Ground new tokens by running\n     `python3 scripts/close-total.py` (idempotent; emits each unresolved token\n     as a first-class meaning under `data/seed/closure-generated-*.lino`) until\n     `python3 scripts/audit-total-closure.py` reports `unresolved_distinct: 0`.\n   - **Worker-mirror parity checks.** Where the JS worker embeds a byte-identical\n     inline mirror of a seed vocabulary, a `--check` guard fails the build on\n     drift (e.g. the “Check terminal vocabulary worker mirror is in sync with\n     seed” CI step runs\n     `node experiments/issue-513-sync-worker-terminal.mjs --check`). Regenerate\n     the mirror by running the same script without `--check`.\n   - **Web-UI hardcoded-string guard (#511).** `npm --prefix tests/e2e run\n     check:web-hardcoded-ui` parses every `h(...)` call in `src/web/app.js` and\n     fails the build when a child argument is a bare prose string literal, so new\n     English text cannot leak into the UI. `npm --prefix tests/e2e run check:i18n`\n     asserts every required key exists in all four locales and that sample\n     interpolations render. When you add a web-UI string: add the key + all four\n     translations in `src/web/i18n-catalog.lino`, register it in `REQUIRED_KEYS`\n     in `tests/e2e/scripts/check-i18n-catalog.mjs`, and render it with `t(...)`.\n\n   See `docs/design/no-hardcoded-natural-language.md` for the full rationale,\n   the meanings ↔ naturalization model, and a worked example.\n\n3. **Roles are declared, then generated.** When you add a meaning with a new\n   `role`, declare it as a `ROLE_*` constant in `src/seed/roles/*.rs`, re-export\n   it from `src/seed.rs`, and regenerate the registry with\n   `python3 scripts/generate-role-registry.py` (keeps `data/seed/roles.lino` in\n   lockstep; enforced by `reference_closure` tests).\n\n4. **Supported-language coverage.** New conversational cues should cover the\n   project's supported languages (currently en, ru, hi, zh). The\n   `tests/e2e/scripts/check-*.mjs` guards fail a one-language change.\n\n5. **Fix everywhere, not just the reported spot.** If a defect has more than one\n   site (most do, because of mirror parity), fix all of them in the one PR.\n\n6. **Reproduce first, then fix.** Add a failing test that reproduces the issue\n   before implementing the fix; a bug fix without a reproducing regression test\n   is treated as incomplete.\n\n7. **When data is insufficient, add tracing.** If there is not enough signal to\n   find a root cause, add debug output / a verbose mode (default **off**) and\n   keep it in the code so the next iteration has the data.\n\n8. **Case study per issue.** Download the issue's logs and data into\n   `docs/case-studies/issue-{id}/` (raw JSON under `raw-data/`) and write a\n   `README.md` that reconstructs the timeline, enumerates every requirement,\n   finds the root cause(s), surveys prior art / existing libraries, and records\n   the implemented fix and its verification.\n\n9. **Report upstream when relevant.** If an issue is rooted in another\n   repository we can file against, open an issue there with a reproducible\n   example, a workaround, and a suggested fix.\n\n10. **One PR per issue.** Plan and execute everything for an issue in a single\n    pull request; commit atomic, individually useful steps so interrupted work\n    stays preserved.\n\n## Pull Request Process\n\n1. //! Natural-language "word problem" normalization extracted from `calculation`

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

/// A normalized arithmetic word problem, ready for calculator evaluation.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct WordProblemNormalization {
    pub expression: String,
    pub reasoning_steps: Vec<String>,
    pub result_label: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum BoxRule {
    Known(i64),
    Multiple { factor: i64, source: String },
    Add { source: String, addend: i64 },
}

/// The `n`-th Fibonacci number under the convention F(1) = F(2) = 1 used across
/// the coding catalog (so F(10) = 55, matching the `fibonacci` program output).
fn fibonacci_value(n: u32) -> u64 {
    if n == 0 {
        return 0;
    }
    let (mut previous, mut current) = (0u64, 1u64);
    for _ in 1..n {
        let next = previous + current;
        previous = current;
        current = next;
    }
    current
}

    if token.is_empty() {
        return None;

#[test]
fn decomposed_sub_results_are_composed_for_algebra() {
    let response =
        synthesis_solver().solve("If x = 2 and y = 5, then what is the value of (x^4 + 2y^2) / 6?");

    assert_eq!(response.intent, "algebra_substitution");
    assert!(response.answer.contains("11"));
    assert!(response
        .evidence_links
        .iter()
        .any(|link| link.starts_with("sub_impulse:")));
    assert!(response
        .evidence_links
        .iter()
        .any(|link| link.starts_with("sub_result:")));
    assert!(response
        .evidence_links
        .iter()
        .any(|link| link.starts_with("composition:substitution:")));
    assert!(response.links_notation.contains("composition:evaluation"));
}

/// Rewrite a natural-language "word problem" into a calculator expression.
///
/// Issue #334 step 2: see the module-level documentation. Returns `None` when
/// no rewrite applies so callers can fall through unchanged.
#[must_use]
pub fn normalize_word_problem_detailed(expression: &str) -> Option<WordProblemNormalization> {
    let trimmed = expression.trim();
    if trimmed.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    if let Some(normalized) = normalize_box_total_problem(trimmed) {
        return Some(normalized);
    }
    // Keep only sentence fragments that carry arithmetic content, dropping pure
    // instruction clauses such as "Show me the code and the final result". The
    // split treats a period as a sentence boundary only when it ends a sentence
    // (followed by whitespace or the end of the string) so decimals like "3.14"
    // survive intact.
    let arithmetic: Vec<String> = split_sentences(trimmed)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|sentence| {
            !sentence.is_empty()
                && (sentence.chars().any(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) || sentence.contains('%'))
        })
        .collect();
    if arithmetic.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let mut working = resolve_fibonacci_references(&arithmetic.join(". "));
    // Rewrite spelled-out operators the calculator does not accept. Longer
    // phrases come first so "and multiply it by" wins over "multiply by".
    for (phrase, symbol) in [
        (" and mult

#[test]
fn fibonacci_convention_matches_catalog() {
    assert_eq!(fibonacci_value(1), 1);
    assert_eq!(fibonacci_value(2), 1);
    assert_eq!(fibonacci_value(5), 5);
    assert_eq!(fibonacci_value(10), 55);
}

#[test]
fn resolves_fibonacci_and_rewrites_operator() {
    // The Fibonacci reference becomes 55, the spelled-out operator becomes
    // `*`, and the trailing instruction sentence is dropped. The leading
    // "calculate" verb is left for the calculator wrapper-stripping stage.
    assert_eq!(
        normalize_word_problem(
            "calculate the 10th Fibonacci number and multiply it by 8% of 500. \
                 Show me the code and the final result."
        )
        .as_deref(),
        Some("calculate 55 * 8% of 500"),
    );
    assert_eq!(
        normalize_word_problem("the fifth Fibonacci number multiplied by 10").as_deref(),
        Some("5 * 10"),
    );
}

#[test]
fn resolves_box_relations_and_total() {
    let normalized = normalize_word_problem_detailed(
        "I have 3 boxes. Box A has twice as many apples as Box B. \
             Box C has 5 more apples than Box A. If Box B has 10 apples, \
             how many apples are there in total? Show your reasoning step by step.",
    )
    .expect("box total problem should normalize");
    assert_eq!(normalized.expression, "20 + 10 + 25");
    assert_eq!(
        normalized.reasoning_steps,
        vec![
            "Box B = 10 apples.",
            "Box A = 2 * 10 = 20 apples.",
            "Box C = 20 + 5 = 25 apples.",
            "Total = 20 + 10 + 25 apples.",
        ],
    );
    assert_eq!(normalized.result_label.as_deref(), Some("apples"));
}

/// Rewrite a natural-language "word problem" into a calculator expression.
///
/// Issue #334 step 2: see the module-level documentation. Returns `None` when
/// no rewrite applies so callers can fall through unchanged.
#[must_use]
pub fn normalize_word_problem_detailed(expression: &str) -> Option<WordProblemNormalization> {
    let trimmed = expression.trim();
    if trimmed.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    if let Some(normalized) = normalize_box_total_problem(trimmed) {
        return Some(normalized);
    }
    // Keep only sentence fragments that carry arithmetic content, dropping pure
    // instruction clauses such as "Show me the code and the final result". The
    // split treats a period as a sentence boundary only when it ends a sentence
    // (followed by whitespace or the end of the string) so decimals like "3.14"
    // survive intact.
    let arithmetic: Vec<String> = split_sentences(trimmed)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|sentence| {
            !sentence.is_empty()
                && (sentence.chars().any(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) || sentence.contains('%'))
        })
        .collect();
    if arithmetic.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let mut working = resolve_fibonacci_references(&arithmetic.join(". "));
    // Rewrite spelled-out operators the calculator does not accept. Longer
    // phrases come first so "and multiply it by" wins over "multiply by".
    for (phrase, symbol) in [
        (" and multiply it by ", " * "),
        (" and multiply by ", " * "),
        (" multiply it by ", " * "),
        ("

use super::*;

#[test]
fn bare_dot_is_detected_only_for_non_decimal_periods() {
    // Issue #334 OOM triggers: a `.` that is not flanked by digits.
    for unsafe_expr in ["2. 3", "2+2. 3+3", "5. 5", ".5", "5.", "2 .3", "a.b"] {
        assert!(
            has_bare_dot(unsafe_expr),
            "{unsafe_expr:?} contains a bare dot and must be rejected"
        );
    }
    // Genuine decimals / dot-grouped digits stay on the link-calculator path.
    for safe_expr in ["3.14", "3.14 + 2.5", "1.000.000", "2024.01.01", "8% of 500"] {
        assert!(
            !has_bare_dot(safe_expr),
            "{safe_expr:?} is a valid decimal expression and must stay safe"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn link_calculator_path_is_skipped_for_bare_dot_expressions() {
    // Before the guard this aborted the process with a multi-GB allocation.
    assert!(evaluate_with_link_calculator("2. 3").is_err());
    assert!(evaluate_with_link_calculator("2+2. 3+3").is_err());
    // Real decimals still reach the upstream calculator and evaluate.
    let evaluation = evaluate_with_link_calculator("3.14 + 2.5").expect("decimal evaluates");
    assert_eq!(evaluation.engine, CalculationEngine::LinkCalculator);
}

use formal_ai::{
    solve, solve_with_history, ConversationTurn, FormalAiEngine, SymbolicAnswer, UniversalSolver,
};

fn answer(prompt: &str) -> SymbolicAnswer {
    FormalAiEngine.answer(prompt)
}

fn has_evidence(response: &SymbolicAnswer, expected: &str) -> bool {
    response
        .evidence_links
        .iter()
        .any(|link| link.starts_with(expected))
}

fn arithmetic_handles_basic_addition() {

    assert_eq!(response.intent, "calculation");
    assert!(response.answer.contains('4'));
    assert!((response.confidence - 1.0).abs() < f32::EPSILON);
}

//! Issue #96: delegate calculator-parsable expressions to link-calculator.
//!
//! These tests cover the formal-ai boundary: natural-language prompt wrappers
//! are stripped in the four currently supported languages, calculator-native
//! expressions are handled by the upstream crate, and local arithmetic remains
//! as a fallback for syntax that calculator does not support yet.

use formal_ai::{ConversationTurn, FormalAiEngine, SymbolicAnswer, UniversalSolver};

fn answer(prompt: &str) -> SymbolicAnswer {
    FormalAiEngine.answer(prompt)
}

fn assert_calculation(prompt: &str, expected_fragments: &[&str]) -> SymbolicAnswer {
    let response = answer(prompt);
    assert_eq!(
        response.intent, "calculation",
        "prompt {prompt:?} should be delegated to calculator, got intent={} answer={}",
        response.intent, response.answer,
    );
    for fragment in expected_fragments {
        assert!(
            response.answer.contains(fragment),
            "prompt {prompt:?} answer should contain {fragment:?}, got {}",
            response.answer,
        );
    }
    response
}

fn assert_calculation_error(prompt: &str, expected_fragments: &[&str]) -> SymbolicAnswer {
    let response = answer(prompt);
    assert_eq!(
        response.intent, "calculation_error",
        "prompt {prompt:?} should report calculator parse failure, got intent={} answer={}",
        response.intent, response.answer,
    );
    for fragment in expected_fragments {
        assert!(
            response.answer.contains(fragment),
            "prompt {prompt:?} answer should contain {fragment:?}, got {}",
            response.answer,
        );
    }
    response
}

fn push_calculation_candidate(
    candidates: &mut Vec<CalculationCandidate>,
    expression: String,
    explicit: bool,
    interpretations: Vec<PromptInterpretation>,
    reasoning_steps: Vec<String>,
    result_label: Option<String>,
) {
    if candidates
        .iter()
        .any(|candidate| candidate.expression == expression)
    {
        return;
    }
    candidates.push(CalculationCandidate {
        expression,
        explicit,
        interpretations,
        reasoning_steps,
        result_label,
    });
}

/// empty vector when the prompt does not look like a calculator request, so
/// the solver can fall through to other specialized handlers.

+         Problem: \"A train leaves Moscow at 60 km/h. Another leaves St. Petersburg at 80 km/h. \
+         Distance: 700 km. When/where do they meet?\"\n\n\
+         Required format:\n\
+         [STEP 1] Define variables -> [VERIFY] Are units consistent?\n\
+         [STEP 2] Write equation -> [VERIFY] Does equation match physics?\n\
+         [STEP 3] Solve algebraically -> [VERIFY] Check arithmetic\n\
+         [STEP 4] Interpret result -> [VERIFY] Does answer make real-world sense?\n\
+         [STEP 5] Convert to user-friendly format (time + location)\n\n\
+         Then: Ask formal-ai to solve the SAME problem, but require it to output verification \
+         tags like above. Compare approaches.",
+    );
+
+    assert_eq!(
+        response.intent, "calculation",
+        "Issue #460 train meeting prompt should not fall through to unknown or calculation_error: {}",
+        response.answer,
+    );
+    for fragment in [
+        "[STEP 1]",
+        "[VERIFY]",
+        "700 / (60 + 80) = 5",
+        "5 hours",
+        "300 km from Moscow",
+        "400 km from St. Petersburg",
+    ] {
+        assert!(
+            response.answer.contains(fragment),
+            "answer should contain {fragment:?}, got {}",

+        );

// operator is rewritten to `*`, and the trailing instruction sentence is
// dropped — yielding `55 * 8% of 500` = 2200. The helpers below mirror
// `fibonacci_value`, `parse_ordinal`, `bare_word`, `resolve_fibonacci_references`,
// `split_sentences` and `normalize_word_problem` in `src/calculation.rs`.
function fibonacciValue(n) {
  if (n === 0) return 0;
  let previous = 0;
  let current = 1;
  for (let step = 1; step < n; step += 1) {
    const next = previous + current;
    previous = current;
    current = next;
  }
  return current;
}

const ORDINAL_WORDS = {
  first: 1,
  second: 2,
  third: 3,
  fourth: 4,
  fifth: 5,
  sixth: 6,
  seventh: 7,
  eighth: 8,
  ninth: 9,
  tenth: 10,
};

// Lowercased, punctuation-trimmed view of a token for keyword comparisons.
function trimNonAlnum(token) {
  return String(token || "")
    .replace(/^[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/u, "")
    .replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}]+$/u, "");
}

function bareWord(token) {
  return trimNonAlnum(token).toLowerCase();
}

// Parse a leading ordinal/cardinal token such as "10th", "10", "3rd" or the
// spelled-out "tenth" into its numeric value. Returns null for anything else.
function parseOrdinal(token) {
  const trimmed = trimNonAlnum(token);
  if (!trimmed) return null;
  const digits = (trimmed.match(/^[0-9]+/) || [""])[0];
  if (digits) {
    const suffix = trimmed.slice(digits.length);
    if (suffix === "" || ["st", "nd", "rd", "th"].includes(suffix)) {
      return Number.parseInt(digits, 10);
    }
    return null;
  }
  const value = ORDINAL_WORDS[trimmed.toLowerCase()];
  return value === undefined ? null : value;
}

+fn parse_decimal_token(token: &str) -> Option<f64> {
+    let cleaned = token.trim_matches(|ch: char| {
+        !(ch.is_ascii_digit() || ch == '.' || ch == '-' || ch == '+')
+    });
+    if cleaned.is_empty()
+        || matches!(cleaned, "." | "-" | "+" | "-." | "+.")
+        || cleaned.chars().filter(|ch| *ch == '.').count() > 1
+    {
+        return None;
+    }
+    cleaned.parse::<f64>().ok()
+}
+
+fn unit_token(token: &str) -> String {
+    token
+        .trim_matches(|ch: char| !(ch.is_alphanumeric() || ch == '/'))
+        .to_ascii_lowercase()
+}
+
+fn is_speed_unit(token: &str) -> bool {
+    matches!(unit_token(token).as_str(), "km/h" | "kph" | "kmh")
+}
+
+fn is_distance_unit(token: &str) -> bool {
+    matches!(
+        unit_token(token).as_str(),
+        "km" | "kilometer" | "kilometers"
+    )
+}
+
+fn format_quantity(value: f64) -> String {
+    if (value - value.round()).abs() < 1e-9 {
+        return format!("{}", value.round() as i64);
+    }
+    let mut formatted = format!("{value:.6}");
+    while formatted.contains('.') && formatted.ends_with('0') {
+        formatted.pop();
+    }
+    if formatted.ends_with('.') {
+        formatted.pop();
+    }
+    formatted
+}
+
+fn clean_origin_token(token: &str, is_last: bool) -> String {
+    let mut cleaned = token
+        .trim_matches(|ch: char| {
+            matches!(
+                ch,
+                '"' | '\'' | '`' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | ',' | ':' | ';'
+            )
+        })
+        .to_owned();
+    if is_last {
+        cleaned = cleaned
+            .trim_end_matches(|ch: char| matches!(ch, '.' | '?' | '!'))
+            .to_owned();
+    }
+    cleaned
+}

+fn extract_origin_before_speed(tokens: &[&str], speed_index: usize, fallback: &str) -> String {
+    let marker = tokens[..speed_index]
+        .iter()
+        .enumerate()
+        .rev()
+        .find(|(_, token)| {
+            matches!(
+                bare_word(token).as_str(),
+                "leaves" | "leave" | "left" | "departs" | "depart" | "starts" | "start"
+            )
+        })
+        .map(|(index, _)| index + 1);
+    let Some(start) = marker else {
+        return fallback.to_owned();
+    };
+    let mut origin_tokens = tokens[start..speed_index].to_vec();
+    while origin_tokens
+        .first()
+        .is_some_and(|token| bare_word(token) == "from")
+    {
+        origin_tokens.remove(0);
+    }
+    while origin_tokens
+        .last()
+        .is_some_and(|token| matches!(bare_word(token).as_str(), "at" | "with"))
+    {
+        origin_tokens.pop();
+    }
+    let cleaned = origin_tokens
+        .iter()
+        .enumerate()
+        .map(|(index, token)| clean_origin_token(token, index + 1 == origin_tokens.len()))
+        .filter(|token| !token.is_empty())
+        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
+        .join(" ");
+    if cleaned.is_empty() {

+fn normalize_train_meeting_problem(text: &str) -> Option<WordProblemNormalization> {
+    let lower = text.to_ascii_lowercase();
+    if !(lower.contains("meet")
+        && (lower.contains("km/h") || lower.contains("kph") || lower.contains("kmh"))
+        && lower.contains("distance"))

+        return None;
+    }

+    let tokens = text.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>();

+    let second_distance = second.value * time;

+    let first_speed_text = format_quantity(first.value);
+    let second_speed_text = format_quantity(second.value);
+    let relative_speed_text = format_quantity(relative_speed);
+    let time_text = format_quantity(time);
+    let first_distance_text = format_quantity(first_distance);

+fn parse_decimal_token(token: &str) -> Option<f64> {
+    let cleaned = token.trim_matches(|ch: char| {
+        !(ch.is_ascii_digit() || ch == '.' || ch == '-' || ch == '+')
+    });
+    if cleaned.is_empty()
+        || matches!(cleaned, "." | "-" | "+" | "-." | "+.")
+        || cleaned.chars().filter(|ch| *ch == '.').count() > 1
+    {
+        return None;
+    }
+    cleaned.parse::<f64>().ok()
+}
+
+fn unit_token(token: &str) -> String {
+    token
+        .trim_matches(|ch: char| !(ch.is_alphanumeric() || ch == '/'))
+        .to_ascii_lowercase()
+}
+
+fn is_speed_unit(token: &str) -> bool {
+    matches!(unit_token(token).as_str(), "km/h" | "kph" | "kmh")
+}
+
+fn is_distance_unit(token: &str) -> bool {
+    matches!(
+        unit_token(token).as_str(),
+        "km" | "kilometer" | "kilometers"
+    )
+}
+
+fn format_quantity(value: f64) -> String {
+    if (value - value.round()).abs() < 1e-9 {
+        return format!("{}", value.round() as i64);
+    }
+    let mut formatted = format!("{value:.6}");
+    while formatted.contains('.') && formatted.ends_with('0') {
+        formatted.pop();
+    }
+    if formatted.ends_with('.') {
+        formatted.pop();
+    }
+    formatted
+}
+
+fn clean_origin_token(token: &str, is_last: bool) -> String {
+    let mut cleaned = token
+        .trim_matches(|ch: char| {
+            matches!(
+                ch,
+                '"' | '\'' | '`' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | ',' | ':' | ';'
+            )
+        })
+        .to_owned();
+    if is_last {
+        cleaned = cleaned
+            .trim_end_matches(|ch: char| matches!(ch, '.' | '?' | '!'))
+            .to_owned();
+    }
+    cleaned
+}
+
+fn extract_origin_before_speed(tokens: &[&str], speed_index: usize, fallback: &str) -> String {
+    let marker = tokens[..speed_index]
+        .iter()
+        .enumerate()
+        .rev()
+        .find(|(_, token)| {
+            matches!(
+                bare_word(token).as_str(),
+                "leaves" | "leave" | "left" | "departs" | "depart" | "starts" | "start"
+            )
+        })
+        .map(|(index, _)| index + 1);
+    let Some(start) = marker else {
+        return fallback.to_owned();
+    };
+    let mut origin_tokens = tokens[start..speed_index].to_vec();
+    while origin_tokens
+        .first()
+        .is_some_and(|token| bare_word(token) == "from")
+    {
+        origin_tokens.remove(0);
+    }
+    while origin_tokens
+        .last()
+        .is_some_and(|token| matches!(bare_word(token).as_str(), "at" | "with"))
+    {
+        origin_tokens.pop();
+    }
+    let cleaned = origin_tokens
+        .iter()
+        .enumerate()
+        .map(|(index, token)| clean_origin_token(token, index + 1 == origin_tokens.len()))
+        .filter(|token| !token.is_empty())
+        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
+        .join(" ");
+    if cleaned.is_empty() {
+        fallback.to_owned()
+    } else {
+        cleaned
+    }
+}

+fn parse_decimal_token(token: &str) -> Option<f64> {
+    let cleaned = token.trim_matches(|ch: char| {
+        !(ch.is_ascii_digit() || ch == '.' || ch == '-' || ch == '+')
+    });
+    if cleaned.is_empty()
+        || matches!(cleaned, "." | "-" | "+" | "-." | "+.")
+        || cleaned.chars().filter(|ch| *ch == '.').count() > 1
+    {
+        return None;
+    }
+    cleaned.parse::<f64>().ok()
+}
+
+fn unit_token(token: &str) -> String {
+    token
+        .trim_matches(|ch: char| !(ch.is_alphanumeric() || ch == '/'))
+        .to_ascii_lowercase()
+}
+
+fn is_speed_unit(token: &str) -> bool {
+    matches!(unit_token(token).as_str(), "km/h" | "kph" | "kmh")
+}
+
+fn is_distance_unit(token: &str) -> bool {
+    matches!(
+        unit_token(token).as_str(),
+        "km" | "kilometer" | "kilometers"
+    )
+}
+
+fn format_quantity(value: f64) -> String {
+    if (value - value.round()).abs() < 1e-9 {
+        return format!("{}", value.round() as i64);
+    }
+    let mut formatted = format!("{value:.6}");
+    while formatted.contains('.') && formatted.ends_with('0') {
+        formatted.pop();
+    }
+    if formatted.ends_with('.') {
+        formatted.pop();
+    }
+    formatted
+}

+fn clean_origin_token(token: &str, is_last: bool) -> String {
+    let mut cleaned = token
+        .trim_matches(|ch: char| {
+            matches!(
+                ch,
+                '"' | '\'' | '`' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | ',' | ':' | ';'

+        })
+        .to_owned();
+    if is_last {
+        cleaned = cleaned
+            .trim_end_matches(|ch: char| matches!(ch, '.' | '?' | '!'))
+            .to_owned();
+    }

+fn extract_origin_before_speed(tokens: &[&str], speed_index: usize, fallback: &str) -> String {
+    let marker = tokens[..speed_index]
+        .iter()
+        .enumerate()
+        .rev()
+        .find(|(_, token)| {
+            matches!(
+                bare_word(token).as_str(),
+                "leaves" | "leave" | "left" | "departs" | "depart" | "starts" | "start"
+            )
+        })
+        .map(|(index, _)| index + 1);
+    let Some(start) = marker else {
+        return fallback.to_owned();
+    };
+    let mut origin_tokens = tokens[start..speed_index].to_vec();
+    while origin_tokens
+        .first()
+        .is_some_and(|token| bare_word(token) == "from")
+    {
+        origin_tokens.remove(0);
+    }
+    while origin_tokens
+        .last()
+        .is_some_and(|token| matches!(bare_word(token).as_str(), "at" | "with"))
+    {
+        origin_tokens.pop();
+    }
+    let cleaned = origin_tokens
+        .iter()
+        .enumerate()
+        .map(|(index, token)| clean_origin_token(token, index + 1 == origin_tokens.len()))
+        .filter(|token| !token.is_empty())
+        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
+        .join(" ");
+    if cleaned.is_empty() {
+        fallback.to_owned()
+    } else {
+        cleaned
+    }

+fn normalize_train_meeting_problem(text: &str) -> Option<WordProblemNormalization> {
+    let lower = text.to_ascii_lowercase();
+    if !(lower.contains("meet")
+        && (lower.contains("km/h") || lower.contains("kph") || lower.contains("kmh"))
+        && lower.contains("distance"))
+    {
+        return None;
+    }
+
+    let tokens = text.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>();
+    let mut speeds = Vec::new();
+    let mut distance = None;
+    for (index, token) in tokens.iter().enumerate() {
+        let Some(value) = parse_decimal_token(token) else {
+            continue;
+        };
+        let Some(unit) = tokens.get(index + 1) else {
+            continue;
+        };

+                "the first start"
+            } else {
+                "the second start"
+            };
+            speeds.push(MotionSpeed {
+                value,
+                origin: extract_origin_before_speed(&tokens, index, fallback),
+            });
+        } else if is_distance_unit(unit) {
+            let preceding = index
+                .checked_sub(1)
+                .and_then(|previous| tokens.get(previous))
+                .map_or_else(String::new, |previous| bare_word(previous));
+            if distance.is_none() || preceding == "distance" {

+            }
+        }

+    if relative_speed <= 0.0 {

+    }

+    let second_distance = second.value * time;

+    let first_speed_text = format_quantity(first.value);
+    let second_speed_text = format_quantity(second.value);
+    let relative_speed_text = format_quantity(relative_speed);

+    let first_distance_text = format_quantity(first_distance);

+fn parse_decimal_token(token: &str) -> Option<f64> {
+    let cleaned = token.trim_matches(|ch: char| {
+        !(ch.is_ascii_digit() || ch == '.' || ch == '-' || ch == '+')
+    });
+    if cleaned.is_empty()
+        || matches!(cleaned, "." | "-" | "+" | "-." | "+.")
+        || cleaned.chars().filter(|ch| *ch == '.').count() > 1
+    {
+        return None;
+    }
+    cleaned.parse::<f64>().ok()
+}
+
+fn unit_token(token: &str) -> String {
+    token
+        .trim_matches(|ch: char| !(ch.is_alphanumeric() || ch == '/'))
+        .to_ascii_lowercase()
+}
+
+fn is_speed_unit(token: &str) -> bool {
+    matches!(unit_token(token).as_str(), "km/h" | "kph" | "kmh")
+}
+
+fn is_distance_unit(token: &str) -> bool {
+    matches!(
+        unit_token(token).as_str(),
+        "km" | "kilometer" | "kilometers"
+    )
+}
+
+fn format_quantity(value: f64) -> String {
+    if (value - value.round()).abs() < 1e-9 {
+        return format!("{}", value.round() as i64);
+    }
+    let mut formatted = format!("{value:.6}");
+    while formatted.contains('.') && formatted.ends_with('0') {
+        formatted.pop();
+    }
+    if formatted.ends_with('.') {
+        formatted.pop();
+    }
+    formatted
+}
+
+fn clean_origin_token(token: &str, is_last: bool) -> String {
+    let mut cleaned = token
+        .trim_matches(|ch: char| {
+            matches!(
+                ch,
+                '"' | '\'' | '`' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | ',' | ':' | ';'
+            )
+        })
+        .to_owned();
+    if is_last {
+        cleaned = cleaned
+            .trim_end_matches(|ch: char| matches!(ch, '.' | '?' | '!'))
+            .to_owned();
+    }
+    cleaned
+}

+function parseMotionDecimalToken(token) {
+  const cleaned = String(token || "")
+    .replace(/^[^0-9.+-]+/, "")
+    .replace(/[^0-9.]+$/, "");
+  if (
+    !cleaned ||
+    cleaned === "." ||
+    cleaned === "-" ||
+    cleaned === "+" ||
+    cleaned === "-." ||
+    cleaned === "+." ||
+    (cleaned.match(/\./g) || []).length > 1
+  ) {
+    return null;
+  }
+  const value = Number.parseFloat(cleaned);
+  return Number.isFinite(value) ? value : null;
+}
+
+function motionUnitToken(token) {
+  return String(token || "")
+    .replace(/^[^\p{L}\p{N}/]+/u, "")
+    .replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}/]+$/u, "")
+    .toLowerCase();
+}
+
+function isMotionSpeedUnit(token) {
+  return ["km/h", "kph", "kmh"].includes(motionUnitToken(token));
+}
+
+function isMotionDistanceUnit(token) {
+  return ["km", "kilometer", "kilometers"].includes(motionUnitToken(token));
+}
+
+function formatMotionQuantity(value) {
+  if (Math.abs(value - Math.round(value)) < 1e-9) {
+    return String(Math.round(value));
+  }
+  return value.toFixed(6).replace(/0+$/, "").replace(/\.$/, "");
+}
+
+function cleanMotionOriginToken(token, isLast) {
+  let cleaned = String(token || "").replace(/^[\"'`()\[\]{},:;]+|[\"'`()\[\]{},:;]+$/g, "");
+  if (isLast) cleaned = cleaned.replace(/[.?!]+$/g, "");
+  return cleaned;
+}
+
+function extractMotionOriginBeforeSpeed(tokens, speedIndex, fallback) {
+  let start = -1;
+  for (let index = speedIndex - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
+    const word = bareWord(tokens[index]);
+    if (
+      word === "leaves" ||
+      word === "leave" ||
+      word === "left" ||
+      word === "departs" ||
+      word === "depart" ||
+      word === "starts" ||
+      word === "start"
+    ) {
+      start = index + 1;
+      break;
+    }
+  }
+  if (start === -1) return fallback;
+  const originTokens = tokens.slice(start, speedIndex);
+  while (originTokens.length > 0 && bareWord(originTokens[0]) === "from") {
+    originTokens.shift();
+  }
+  while (
+    originTokens.length > 0 &&
+    (bareWord(originTokens[originTokens.length - 1]) === "at" ||
+      bareWord(originTokens[originTokens.length - 1]) === "with")
+  ) {
+    originTokens.pop();
+  }
+  const cleaned = originTokens
+    .map((token, index) => cleanMotionOriginToken(token, index + 1 === originTokens.length))
+    .filter(Boolean)
+    .join(" ");
+  return cleaned || fallback;
+}
+
+function normalizeTrainMeetingProblem(text) {
+  const source = String(text || "");
+  const lower = source.toLowerCase();
+  if (
+    !lower.includes("meet") ||
+    !(lower.includes("km/h") || lower.includes("kph") || lower.includes("kmh")) ||
+    !lower.includes("distance")
+  ) {
+    return null;
+  }
+
+  const tokens = source.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
+  const speeds = [];
+  let distance = null;
+  for (let index = 0; index < tokens.length; index += 1) {
+    const value = parseMotionDecimalToken(tokens[index]);
+    if (value === null || tokens[index + 1] === undefined) continue;
+    if (isMotionSpeedUnit(tokens[index + 1])) {
+      const fallback = speeds.length === 0 ? "the first start" : "the second start";
+      speeds.push({
+        value,
+        origin: extractMotionOriginBeforeSpeed(tokens, index, fallback),
+      });
+    } else if (isMotionDistanceUnit(tokens[index + 1])) {
+      const preceding = index > 0 ? bareWord(tokens[index - 1]) : "";
+      if (distance === null || preceding === "distance") {
+        distance = value;
+      }
+    }
+  }
+  if (speeds.length < 2 || distance === null) return null;
+
+  const first = speeds[0];
+  const second = speeds[1];
+  const relativeSpeed = first.value + second.value;
+  if (!(relativeSpeed > 0)) return null;
+  const time = distance / relativeSpeed;
+  const firstDistance = first.value * time;
+  const secondDistance = second.value * time;
+
+  const distanceText = formatMotionQuantity(distance);
+  const firstSpeedText = formatMotionQuantity(first.value);
+  const secondSpeedText = formatMotionQuantity(second.value);
+  const relativeSpeedText = formatMotionQuantity(relativeSpeed);
+  const timeText = formatMotionQuantity(time);
+  const firstDistanceText = formatMotionQuantity(firstDistance);
+  const secondDistanceText = formatMotionQuantity(secondDistance);
+  const expression = `${distanceText} / (${firstSpeedText} + ${secondSpeedText})`;
+
+  return {
+    expression,
+    reasoningSteps: [
+      `[STEP 1] Define variables: distance = ${distanceText} km, ${first.origin} train speed = ${firstSpeedText} km/h, ${second.origin} train speed = ${secondSpeedText} km/h, and t = meeting time in hours. [VERIFY] Units are consistent: kilometers divided by kilometers per hour gives hours.`,
+      `[STEP 2] Write equation: (${firstSpeedText} + ${secondSpeedText}) * t = ${distanceText}. [VERIFY] The trains move toward each other, so their relative speed is ${relativeSpeedText} km/h.`,
+      `[STEP 3] Solve algebraically: t = ${distanceText} / (${firstSpeedText} + ${secondSpeedText}) = ${timeText} hours. [VERIFY] ${firstSpeedText} + ${secondSpeedText} = ${relativeSpeedText} and ${distanceText} / ${relativeSpeedText} = ${timeText}.`,
+      `[STEP 4] Interpret result: the ${first.origin} train travels ${firstSpeedText} * ${timeText} = ${firstDistanceText} km; the ${second.origin} train travels ${secondSpeedText} * ${timeText} = ${secondDistanceText} km. [VERIFY] ${firstDistanceText} + ${secondDistanceText} = ${distanceText} km.`,
+      `[STEP 5] Convert to user-friendly format: they meet after ${timeText} hours, ${firstDistanceText} km from ${first.origin} and ${secondDistanceText} km from ${second.origin}. [VERIFY] Both distances add to the stated route length.`,
+      "[COMPARE] Formal-ai uses the same relative-speed equation as the direct solution; the verification tags make each assumption and arithmetic check explicit.",
+    ],
+    resultLabel: "",
+  };

// Issue #27: greeting randomisation defaults to ON in production. Tests pin
// the canonical greeting text so they assert deterministic output; new tests
// that actually exercise the randomisation flip the preference back on.
async function disableGreetingVariations(page) {
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    try {
      window.localStorage.setItem(
        'formal-ai.preferences.v1',
        'demo_preferences\n  greetingVariations "off"',
      );
    } catch (_error) {
      // localStorage may be unavailable; tests will tolerate variant text.
    }
  });
}

async function sendPrompt(page, text) {
  const input = page.locator('[data-testid="chat-composer-input"]');
  await expect(input).toBeEnabled({ timeout: 5_000 });
  await input.fill(text);
  return submitCurrentPrompt(page);
}

async function submitCurrentPrompt(page) {
  const messages = page.locator('[data-testid="chat-message"]');
  const initialCount = await messages.count();
  await page.locator('[data-testid="chat-composer-submit"]').click();
  await expect(messages).toHaveCount(initialCount + 2, { timeout: 20_000 });
  const lastMsg = messages.last();
  await expect(lastMsg).toHaveClass(/assistant/);
  return lastMsg;
}

async function sendPrompt(page, text) {
  const input = page.locator('[data-testid="chat-composer-input"]');
  await expect(input).toBeEnabled({ timeout: 5_000 });
  await input.fill(text);
  const messages = page.locator('[data-testid="chat-message"]');
  const initial = await messages.count();
  await page.locator('[data-testid="chat-composer-submit"]').click();
  await expect(messages).toHaveCount(initial + 2, { timeout: 20_000 });
  return messages.last();
}

async function routeFramePolicy(page, headers) {
  const requests = [];
  await page.route('**://api.microlink.io/**', async (route) => {
    requests.push(route.request().url());
    await route.fulfill({
      status: 200,
      contentType: 'application/json',
      headers: { 'access-control-allow-origin': '*' },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        status: 'success',
        statusCode: 200,
        headers,
      }),
    });
  });
  return requests;
}

async function setRangeValue(page, testId, value) {
  await page.locator(`[data-testid="${testId}"]`).evaluate((node, nextValue) => {
    const valueSetter = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(
      Object.getPrototypeOf(node),
      'value',
    )?.set;
    valueSetter.call(node, String(nextValue));
    node.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
    node.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true }));
  }, value);
}

+// @ts-check
+//
+// Issue #460: the browser WASM-worker demo routed a train meeting word problem
+// with explicit verification-format instructions to the unknown fallback. This
+// spec drives the real browser bundle and pins the relative-speed solution.
+const { test, expect } = require('@playwright/test');
+
+const REPORTED_PROMPT =
+  'Solve this step-by-step, but with verification at each stage:\n\n' +
+  'Problem: "A train leaves Moscow at 60 km/h. Another leaves St. Petersburg at 80 km/h. ' +
+  'Distance: 700 km. When/where do they meet?"\n\n' +
+  'Required format:\n' +
+  '[STEP 1] Define variables -> [VERIFY] Are units consistent?\n' +
+  '[STEP 2] Write equation -> [VERIFY] Does equation match physics?\n' +
+  '[STEP 3] Solve algebraically -> [VERIFY] Check arithmetic\n' +
+  '[STEP 4] Interpret result -> [VERIFY] Does answer make real-world sense?\n' +
+  '[STEP 5] Convert to user-friendly format (time + location)\n\n' +
+  'Then: Ask formal-ai to solve the SAME problem, but require it to output verification ' +
+  'tags like above. Compare approaches.';
+
+async function sendPrompt(page, text) {
+  const input = page.locator('[data-testid="chat-composer-input"]');
+  await expect(input).toBeEnabled({ timeout: 5_000 });
+  await input.fill(text);
+
+  const messages = page.locator('[data-testid="chat-message"]');
+  const initialCount = await messages.count();
+  await page.locator('[data-testid="chat-composer-submit"]').click();
+  await expect(messages).toHaveCount(initialCount + 2, { timeout: 20_000 });
+
+  const assistantMessage = messages.last();
+  await expect(assistantMessage).toHaveClass(/assistant/);
+  await expect(assistantMessage.locator('.markdown-body')).toBeVisible();
+  return assistantMessage;
+}
+
+test.describe('Issue #460 - train meeting word problem', () => {
+  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
+    await page.addInitScript(() => {
+      window.localStorage.setItem(
+        'formal-ai.preferences.v1',
+        'demo_preferences\n  demoMode "off"\n  diagnosticsMode "on"\n  greetingVariations "off"',
+      );
+    });
+    await page.goto('./');
+    await expect(page.locator('.app')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15_000 });
+    await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="demo-status"]')).toHaveText('Manual mode');
+    await expect(page.locator('.status')).toContainText('wasm worker');
+  });
+
+  test('answers with verification-tagged relative-speed reasoning', async ({ page }) => {
+    const message = await sendPrompt(page, REPORTED_PROMPT);
+
+    for (const fragment of [
+      '[STEP 1]',
+      '[VERIFY]',
+      '700 / (60 + 80) = 5',
+      '5 hours',
+      '300 km from Moscow',
+      '400 km from St. Petersburg',
+      '[COMPARE]',
+    ]) {
+      await expect(message).toContainText(fragment);
+    }
+
+    await expect(message).not.toContainText('could not evaluate it');
+    await expect(message).not.toContainText('cannot answer that from local links rules');
+  });
+});

# Case study - Issue #441: "Unknown prompt: Что такое vulkan layer"

- **Issue:** [#441](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/441)
- **Reported version:** 0.190.0 (WASM worker), GitHub Pages, mobile Firefox
- **Reported prompt:** `Что такое vulkan layer`
- **Reported result:** `intent: unknown`
- **Pull request:** [#473](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/473)
- **Raw data:** [`raw-data/`](./raw-data/) contains the issue JSON, issue comments, and PR metadata captured for this fix.

## What Happened

The prompt starts with the Russian definition cue `Что такое`, then asks about
the Latin technical term `vulkan layer`. The reported reasoning trace showed the
formalization was correct:

```text
(@USER OP:define ?vulkan layer)
```

But the worker detected `language:en` because the Latin letters in `vulkan layer`
outnumbered the Cyrillic letters in `Что такое`. The prompt then fell through the
lookup chain and returned the English unknown-intent fallback.

## Root Cause

`src/language.rs` and the mirrored browser worker detector both used raw script
letter counts. That works for monolingual prompts, but fails for localized
definition prompts that include Latin product names, APIs, packages, or graphics
terms. In these cases the leading prompt language carries the user's command,
while the Latin span is the thing being asked about.

The Rust and JS paths had the same behavior, so the fix had to preserve parity.

## Fix

Language detection now records the first alphabetic script and checks for
supported-language question markers. When a prompt starts in a supported
non-Latin script, or when a term-first prompt includes local question words, the
detector preserves that prompt language even if the Latin term has more letters.
The existing dominant-script fallback still handles monolingual and other
mixed-script cases.

The change is mirrored in:

- `src/languag

# Issue 461 - Russian PHP Hello World Follow-Up

## Timeline

- 2026-06-13: A Russian web user asked `Что ты умеешь делать?`; the assistant
  advertised Hello World generation, then answered `unknown` to
  `На php не получится написать?`.
- 2026-06-26: The issue was reproduced with a native integration test that
  replays the capabilities answer as conversation history.

## Requirements

- The follow-up must not fall through to `unknown`.
- The prompt must inherit the Hello World task from the preceding capabilities
  context.
- PHP must be answered through the existing cached coding oracle, preserving
  source attribution to the Hello World Collection.
- Rust and the browser worker recognizers must remain in parity.

## Root Cause

The write-program formalizer only routed a prompt when the current turn named a
task such as `hello world`, or combined a program-kind noun with a program-request
verb. The reported follow-up named a known oracle language (`php`) and a request
verb (`написать`), but no program noun or task. Because the turn never became an
unsupported `write_program` request, context recovery could not inherit the
Hello World task from the capabilities answer and the oracle was never tried.

## Prior Work

Issue 412 added the cached coding oracle for languages outside the verified
catalog, including PHP. Issue 324 added context recovery for incomplete
write-program follow-ups. This fix connects those existing pieces by allowing a
request verb plus a catalog/oracle-known language to enter the same recovery
path.

## Fix

- Rust `write_program_parameters` now accepts prompts that mention a
  `program_request` verb and a language known by either the verified catalog or
  the cached coding oracle.
- `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` mirrors the same predicate with the worker's
  local catalog and oracle cache.
- A regression test covers the exact Russian dialog

*** Add File: /tmp/gh-issue-solver-1782469135481/docs/case-studies/issue-460/README.md
+# Case study - Issue #460: train meeting word problem with verification tags
+
+- **Issue:** [#460](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/460)
+- **Reported version:** 0.194.0 (WASM worker), GitHub Pages
+- **Reported prompt:** `Solve this step-by-step, but with verification at each stage: ... A train leaves Moscow at 60 km/h ...`
+- **Reported result:** `intent: unknown`
+- **Pull request:** [#570](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/570)
+- **Raw data:** [`raw-data/`](./raw-data/) contains the issue JSON, issue comments, and PR metadata captured for this fix.
+
+## Timeline
+
+- 2026-06-13: The browser WASM worker reported the train meeting prompt as
+  `intent: unknown`.
+- 2026-06-26: The prepared branch reproduced the same missing capability as a
+  `calculation_error`: newer arithmetic-cue handling noticed `Solve`, but still
+  sent the whole instruction-heavy prompt to the calculator without a word
+  problem rewrite.
+
+## Root Cause
+
+The calculator already handled explicit arithmetic and a few natural-language
+word-problem rewrites, but it had no normalizer for opposing-motion train
+meeting problems. The prompt also included required output-format instructions
+and a compare request, so the generic arithmetic extractor could not reduce it
+to the core equation:
+
+```text
+700 / (60 + 80)
+```
+
+Rust and the browser worker keep parallel arithmetic logic, so the fix had to be
+mirrored in both implementations.
+
+## Fix
+
+- Added a train meeting word-problem normalizer that extracts two km/h speeds,
+  the route distance, and the departure origins.
+- The normalizer computes relative speed, meeting time, and each train's
+  traveled distance, then returns verification-tagged reasoning steps matching
+  the requested format.
+- Reasoning-step rendering now preserves steps that already start with a tag
+  such as `[STEP 1]` instead of prepending an extra `Step N:`.
+- Mirrored the Rust behavior in `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` for browser WASM
+  parity.
+
+## Verification
+
+- Before the fix, `cargo test --test unit arithmetic_solves_train_meeting_problem_with_verification_tags -- --nocapture`
+  failed with `calculation_error`.
+- `cargo test --test source resolves_train_meeting_problem_with_verification_steps -- --nocapture`
+- `cargo test --test unit arithmetic_solves_train_meeting_problem_with_verification_tags -- --nocapture`
+- `node --check src/web/formal_ai_worker.js`
+- `npx playwright test --config=playwright.local.config.js issue-460.spec.js`
*** End Patch

+# Case study - Issue #460: train meeting word problem with verification tags
+
+- **Issue:** [#460](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/460)
+- **Reported version:** 0.194.0 (WASM worker), GitHub Pages
+- **Reported prompt:** `Solve this step-by-step, but with verification at each stage: ... A train leaves Moscow at 60 km/h ...`
+- **Reported result:** `intent: unknown`
+- **Pull request:** [#570](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/570)
+- **Raw data:** [`raw-data/`](./raw-data/) contains the issue JSON, issue comments, and PR metadata captured for this fix.
+
+## Timeline
+
+- 2026-06-13: The browser WASM worker reported the train meeting prompt as
+  `intent: unknown`.
+- 2026-06-26: The prepared branch reproduced the same missing capability as a
+  `calculation_error`: newer arithmetic-cue handling noticed `Solve`, but still
+  sent the whole instruction-heavy prompt to the calculator without a word
+  problem rewrite.
+
+## Root Cause
+
+The calculator already handled explicit arithmetic and a few natural-language
+word-problem rewrites, but it had no normalizer for opposing-motion train
+meeting problems. The prompt also included required output-format instructions
+and a compare request, so the generic arithmetic extractor could not reduce it
+to the core equation:
+
+```text
+700 / (60 + 80)
+```
+
+Rust and the browser worker keep parallel arithmetic logic, so the fix had to be
+mirrored in both implementations.
+
+## Fix
+
+- Added a train meeting word-problem normalizer that extracts two km/h speeds,
+  the route distance, and the departure origins.
+- The normalizer computes relative speed, meeting time, and each train's
+  traveled distance, then returns verification-tagged reasoning steps matching
+  the requested format.
+- Reasoning-step rendering now preserves steps that already start with a tag
+  such as `[STEP 1]` instead of prepending an extra `Step N:`.
+- Mirrored the Rust behavior in `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` for browser WASM
+  parity.
+
+## Verification
+
+- Before the fix, `cargo test --test unit arithmetic_solves_train_meeting_problem_with_verification_tags -- --nocapture`
+  failed with `calculation_error`.
+- `cargo test --test source resolves_train_meeting_problem_with_verification_steps -- --nocapture`
+- `cargo test --test unit arithmetic_solves_train_meeting_problem_with_verification_tags -- --nocapture`
+- `node --check src/web/formal_ai_worker.js`
+- `npx playwright test --config=playwright.local.config.js issue-460.spec.js`
*** End Patch

+#[test]
+fn arithmetic_embedded_requests_stay_available_across_supported_languages() {
+    struct Case {
+        language: &'static str,
+        prompt: &'static str,
+        expected: &'static str,
+    }
+
+    let cases = [
+        Case {
+            language: "en",
+            prompt: "I want to know what is 2+2",
+            expected: "2+2 = 4",
+        },
+        Case {
+            language: "ru",
+            prompt: "хочу понять сколько будет 2+2",
+            expected: "2+2 = 4",
+        },
+        Case {
+            language: "hi",
+            prompt: "मुझे बताओ गणना करें 8 / 2",
+            expected: "8 / 2 = 4",
+        },
+        Case {
+            language: "zh",
+            prompt: "我想知道计算 2 + 2",
+            expected: "2 + 2 = 4",
+        },
+    ];
+
+    for case in cases {
+        let response = answer(case.prompt);
+        assert_eq!(
+            response.intent, "calculation",
+            "language {} prompt should route to calculation: {}",
+            case.language, response.answer
+        );
+        assert!(
+            has_evidence(&response, &format!("language:{}", case.language)),
+            "language {} should be recorded in evidence: {:?}",
+            case.language,
+            response.evidence_links
+        );
+        assert!(
+            response.answer.contains(case.expected),
+            "language {} answer should contain {:?}, got {}",
+            case.language,
+            case.expected,
+            response.answer
+        );
+    }
+}
